## Fixed

`structured` markdown reads three layouts it misread in an unseen city's
comprehensive plan (Harrah, Oklahoma, 2018).

- A column whose paragraphs each open with a styled heading ("Rural Estate",
  "Single-Family", …) is running text, so a three-column page splits into its
  columns instead of reading across them. Headings are left out of the count
  only while they are at most half the column's lines, and among equally wide
  gutters the one nearest the middle of the page splits it, so a two-column
  plan page is not cut one column in.
- A title set as upright letters stepping down or up the margin (a chapter
  banner, a map sheet's running head) reads as one upright line, also when it
  sits in a text box. It read as a table of single letters.
- A weight a font does not declare but pdfium estimates (Georgia at 665) no
  longer makes its text bold when the font's name says which face it is.
  Body text of such a font was marked bold throughout.

The text bench stays at 1204 of 1204 checks (Docling 853, `pdftotext -layout`
378), and all fourteen reviewed dossiers are unchanged. Across the corpus, eight
pages read differently from 0.18.2: seven lose bold marks their print does not
have, and one reads its footer in order.
